headline: 英美藝文評論精選
context: 愛丁堡藝穗節（Edinburgh Fringe）本週有兩齣新戲登場評論，書評版推薦了兩本新的犯罪驚悚小說，墨爾本一部關於電話詐騙的新片也上了影評版。

sources.name: The Guardian
sources.summary: Summerhall, Edinburgh Fadi Murad’s unconventional drama is a collage structured with the free-form imagination of a poet Last year, a group of Scottish producers staged a four-day mini festival called Welcome to the Fringe, Palestine . One of the excerpts was a scratch performance by Fadi Murad, which now returns as a full-length show. It is not a conventional drama. Rather, Come Back Home is structured with the free-ranging imagination of a poet, an impressionistic collage that resists straightforward interpretation. Murad’s theme is one of loss and the pull of home, focusing in particular on the death of his mother in a car accident when he was nine. He speaks touchingly from a child’s perspective of what it meant to lose the nurturer in his life, the one he turned to in just such a moment of distress. And he shares video footage of his younger self singing Mad World by Tears for Fears at her memorial. It is as cute as it is sad. At Summerhall, Edinburgh , until 31 August All our Edinburgh festival reviews Continue reading...
sources.title: Come Back Home review – loss and love in Palestinian artist’s intriguing fringe hour

sources.name: The Guardian
sources.summary: theSpace Triplex, Edinburgh Four skaters enter into feral competition in this darkly funny yet flimsily plotted play about female teenhood The title refers to the figure-skating legend and Olympian who, in the noughties, captivated the US with her performances on ice, winning a total of five world championships. Here, the four teen skaters trying to make it big worship her, quite literally, invoking her for strength on and off the ice. It is a great central idea with moments of frozen action as each girl sends a wish, a fear or prayer up to a godlike, absent Kwan in their most anxious or exhilarated moments. Christie Spessard’s play has verve, capturing the extremes of adolescent life and competitive sport. Energetically directed by Ryan Pangracs, it is full of humour with some zingers and movement that contains a true sense of gliding. At theSpace Triplex, Edinburgh , until 29 August All our Edinburgh festival reviews Continue reading...

sources.name: The Guardian
sources.summary: The Amateur by Chris Bohjalian; Claws Out! by Bella Mackie; Plant Lady by Minyoung Kang; Children of Wolves by Lawrence Osborne; Mad Mabel by Sally Hepworth The Amateur by Chris Bohjalian (Hutchinson Heinemann, £18.99) American bestseller Bohjalian deserves to be far better known in the UK, although, as the first line of his 26th novel points out, “It is neither virtue nor might that rules the world; it’s luck”. Mira Winston’s luck began early, as she was born into a rich family, clever enough to secure a place at Yale, and a talented enough golfer to consider turning pro, but things change dramatically in 1978 when, at the age of 18, a ball she hits on a driving range smashes the temporal bone of a young caddy, killing him almost instantly. The freak accident turns out to be rather more complicated than first thought, not least because it becomes karmically conflated, in Mira’s mind, with her relationship with a married man twice her age. Told as a memoir, with Mira looking back on the derailment of her life and chronicling society’s changing perceptions of agency and privilege, this literary thriller is a masterfully executed ace. Claws Out! by Bella Mackie (Borough, £20) Mackie’s third novel centres on Diana, a manipulative grifter whose previous three husbands have died, apparently of natural causes. She’s in the process of getting her feet under the fourth mark’s prosperous Hampstead table when she encounters opposition. David Farrand’s “entitled but otherwise entirely average” daughter Catriona isn’t going to give up her father or her inheritance without a fight, and when she starts investigating Diana’s past, she discovers that her former stepchildren are convinced of foul play. Meanwhile, Diana’s own son, a feckless charmer, is also hoping to benefit from his mother’s matrimonial plans. Some readers may find the arch authorial tone grating, and the sharp-eyed will spot at least one major plot development before it occurs, but the incisive social satire, vinegary humour and expert pacing will keep you laughing as you turn the pages. sources.name: The Guardian
sources.summary: In Hollywood’s hands this would be a pulse-pounding thriller, but Maddelin McKenna’s lithe feature debut is all about street-level authenticity There are few films that feel as quintessentially “Melbourne” as Mad Rush, the feature debut of writer-director Maddelin McKenna. It largely unfolds in the city’s centre, with a scaled-back colour palette – lots of blues and greys – that seems informed by the city itself. McKenna brings a grainy street-level authenticity to a story centred on gen Z protagonist Madisha (Senuri Chandrani), who is targeted by an intricate phone scam involving callers who claim to work for the Australian tax office and insist she withdraw all cash from her bank account. In Hollywood’s hands this premise would probably become a pulse-pounding thriller. Here, it more closely follows the beats of a far more realistic “day in the life of” narrative. Its small conversation-based moments are convincingly staged, but don’t do much to service the plot or propel things forward, although the pacing remains quite tight across the run time’s lithe 76 minutes. sources.title: Mad Rush review – an intricate phone scam isn’t quite enough to drive this very Melbourne movie

thread_text:
愛丁堡藝穗節（Edinburgh Fringe）本週有兩齣新戲登場評論。巴勒斯坦藝術家法迪・穆拉德（Fadi Murad）的獨角戲《Come Back Home》，用詩意的拼貼手法，講述他九歲那年母親車禍過世的故事；另一齣《Dear Michelle Kwan》則是花式滑冰喜劇，四名少女滑冰選手把偶像米雪兒・關（Michelle Kwan）當成心靈寄託。

書評版本週推薦了兩本犯罪驚悚小說：克里斯・波哈利安（Chris Bohjalian）的新作《The Amateur》，寫一場高爾夫球意外如何改變一名女子的一生；貝拉・麥基（Bella Mackie）的《Claws Out!》，則講一名靠婚姻斂財、三任丈夫先後過世的女子。

墨爾本電影《Mad Rush》，描寫一名Z世代女子遭遇假冒稅務機關的電話詐騙，導演捨棄好萊塢式的緊張刺激，改用寫實的生活步調呈現整起事件。

—— 本則整理自 The Guardian 於 2026 年 8 月 14 日發佈的報導，讓圖書館員翻譯給你聽。

voice_text:
愛丁堡藝穗節，這週有兩齣新戲上場。巴勒斯坦藝術家法迪・穆拉德（Fadi Murad）的獨角戲《Come Back Home》，用詩意拼貼的手法，講他九歲那年母親車禍過世的故事。另一齣《Dear Michelle Kwan》，是花式滑冰喜劇，四名少女滑冰選手，把偶像米雪兒・關當成心靈寄託。

書評這邊，本週推薦了兩本犯罪驚悚小說。克里斯・波哈利安的新作《The Amateur》，寫一場高爾夫球意外，如何改變一名女子的一生。貝拉・麥基的《Claws Out!》，講一名靠婚姻斂財、三任丈夫先後過世的女子。

電影方面，墨爾本新片《Mad Rush》，描寫一名Z世代女子，遭遇假冒稅務機關的電話詐騙。導演捨棄了好萊塢式的緊張刺激，改用寫實的生活步調，呈現整起事件。
